units.title: ASI Is a Stack, Not a Model
units.narrative_job: Replace the image of a single superintelligent model with a system of distinct responsibilities and governed transitions, then establish noninheritance as the book's central engineering law.
units.central_question: What must remain separate for advanced intelligence to be understandable, governable, repairable, and replaceable?
units.strongest_objection: Explicit layers may discard useful information and create ceremony that a capable end-to-end model could avoid.
units.conclusion_change: Matched natural deployments in which a simpler monolith is equally controllable, observable, recoverable, useful, and affordable would narrow or reject parts of the stack thesis.
units.handoff: Separation has a cost, so Unit 2 asks whether routing, reuse, and specialization can pay for the architecture rather than merely decorate it.

units.title: The Efficient ASI Hypothesis
units.narrative_job: State the book's efficiency hypothesis without treating token reduction, benchmark speed, or smaller models as automatic system-level improvement.
units.central_question: Can a governed stack produce more accepted useful work per unit of total lifecycle cost than frontier-model-only operation?
units.strongest_objection: Governance and routing overhead may exceed any savings from specialization or reuse.
units.conclusion_change: Full-cost matched workloads showing no risk-adjusted quality, throughput, or recovery advantage would reject or sharply narrow the hypothesis.
units.handoff: Efficiency is meaningful only inside an authority boundary, which Unit 3 develops through concrete failure and misuse cases.

units.title: Authority, Failure, and Misuse
units.narrative_job: Show why proposing, approving, executing, observing, and releasing are different acts, then pressure-test that distinction against ordinary failure, dual-use uplift, and high-consequence domains.
units.central_question: Who may cause which effect, under what conditions, and who owns the result when capability outruns authority or observation?
units.strongest_objection: Typed authority can become ceremonial metadata when the runtime, operator, or institution can bypass it.
units.conclusion_change: Simpler permission systems that resist revocation, bypass, confused-deputy, escalation, and residual-loss failures equally well would justify a smaller boundary model.
units.handoff: Authority cannot survive an untrusted substrate, so Unit 4 moves downward into security, privacy, computation, and artifact custody.

units.title: Security, Privacy, and AI Artifact Custody
units.narrative_job: Establish the trusted base beneath cognitive governance and follow data, models, dependencies, keys, attestations, and release decisions through their distinct custody lifecycles.
units.central_question: What must remain outside the model so that untrusted content, compromised components, private data, and irreversible releases do not silently acquire authority?
units.strongest_objection: Hardware roots, attestations, provenance records, and policy kernels can all be compromised or produce false assurance about the larger system.
units.conclusion_change: Evidence that a materially smaller trusted base preserves confidentiality, integrity, revocation, provenance, and post-release risk at lower burden would narrow the design.
units.handoff: Secure records still do not tell us what to believe, so Unit 5 turns from custody to evidence and scalable review.

units.title: Evidence States and Scalable Oversight
units.narrative_job: Explain how support changes without laundering nearby claims, then connect scalable oversight and internal-model evidence to the same identity-bound discipline.
units.central_question: How can limited evaluators learn from behavior, internal signals, proofs, and delegated review without letting any one artifact stand in for truth or safety?
units.strongest_objection: Evidence labels and oversight hierarchies may create an aura of rigor while dependence, weak constructs, and reviewer incapacity remain unchanged.
units.conclusion_change: Natural correction streams in which simpler review records produce equal calibration, challenge, and error recovery would justify a smaller transition system.
units.handoff: Oversight itself can be manipulated or misunderstand intent, so Unit 6 centers the human as principal, reviewer, and epistemic target.

units.title: Human Intent, Control, and Epistemic Security
units.narrative_job: Turn human intent from an assumed prompt property into a revisable formal input while accounting for attention, comprehension, persuasion, disagreement, revocation, and the cost of meaningful control.
units.central_question: How does an ambiguous human request become bounded work without inventing permission or manipulating the person who must approve it?
units.strongest_objection: Formal intent contracts can harden a mistaken interpretation and shift genuine human judgment into unread fields.
units.conclusion_change: User studies showing lighter clarification and control mechanisms produce fewer consequential intent and manipulation failures at lower burden would narrow the contract.
units.handoff: Individual intent cannot settle conflicting values, so Unit 7 moves from commands to constitutions and objective formation.

units.title: Constitutions, Moral Uncertainty, and Objective Formation
units.narrative_job: Show how protected commitments, unresolved value conflict, learned objectives, amendment, and appeal can coexist without allowing an optimizer to ratify its own purpose.
units.central_question: How should a system act when objectives are learned, values conflict, and no single preference can legitimately settle the case?
units.strongest_objection: A formal constitution may freeze contested values, centralize power, and provide only the appearance of alignment.
units.conclusion_change: Pluralistic mechanisms with fewer capture, rigidity, evasion, and review-burden failures would replace or sharply narrow the proposed substrate.
units.handoff: Constitutions need legitimate institutions, which Unit 8 treats as an engineering dependency rather than an assumed source of authority.

units.title: Institutions, Coordination, and Societal Resilience
units.narrative_job: Extend governance from one system to affected publics, jurisdictions, competing organizations, international coordination, remedy, and recovery under diffuse or cumulative harm.
units.central_question: What makes an AI governance decision legitimate and resilient when authority, harms, and affected parties cross institutional boundaries?
units.strongest_objection: Institutional machinery can entrench incumbents, diffuse accountability, and move more slowly than the harms it governs.
units.conclusion_change: Leaner institutional designs that preserve standing, remedy, coordination, and recovery with less capture and delay would justify consolidation.
units.handoff: Part II begins by asking how stable technical capabilities can change behind these governance boundaries without inheriting readiness.

units.title: Stable Capability Fields and Governed Replacement
units.narrative_job: Separate stable capability identity from changing implementation identity and make qualification, migration, rollback, and retirement properties of each replacement rather than inherited reputation.
units.central_question: How can a system change its models, tools, memories, and substrates without losing the contract that makes those changes governable?
units.strongest_objection: Stable field names can hide semantic drift and make incomparable components appear interchangeable.
units.conclusion_change: Natural replacement studies showing no continuity, challenge, or recovery benefit beyond conventional versioning would weaken the abstraction.
units.handoff: A replaceable capability must still know what happened, so Unit 10 starts the cognitive path with observation trust.

units.title: Perception and Observation Trust
units.narrative_job: Establish observations as provenance-bearing, fallible inputs rather than direct reality, then extend that discipline to real-time physical control where latency and irreversible effects matter.
units.central_question: When may a system treat sensor, tool, human, or environmental reports as independent-enough evidence about actual state?
units.strongest_objection: Provenance fields cannot guarantee independence, calibration, or physical truth and may merely document correlated error.
units.conclusion_change: Simpler fusion and control systems with equal calibration, contradiction detection, latency, and recovery would justify a thinner trust model.
units.handoff: Observations become useful when organized into predictions and causal alternatives, which Unit 11 assigns to governed world models.

units.title: Governed World Models and Reality Grounding
units.narrative_job: Keep simulations, predictions, interventions, observations, and reconciled beliefs distinct while showing how their mismatch drives useful learning and control.
units.central_question: How can a system reason over possible worlds without confusing a successful simulation or plausible story with actual state?
units.strongest_objection: World-model governance may add records without improving prediction, causal identification, calibration, or action.
units.conclusion_change: Strong predictive and causal baselines with simpler branch discipline and equal intervention value would justify collapsing the extra machinery.
units.handoff: A world model can compare futures, but Unit 12 must decide how a plan coordinates them without becoming permission.

units.title: Planning as a Control Layer
units.narrative_job: Treat plans as versioned, challengeable control artifacts that coordinate dependencies and alternatives without granting execution authority.
units.central_question: How can a plan remain useful when assumptions, context, costs, and authority change during execution?
units.strongest_objection: Detailed plans can be expensive and brittle in environments that change faster than they can be checked.
units.conclusion_change: Dynamic-task studies in which direct reactive control is safer, cheaper, and more recoverable would narrow when explicit planning should activate.
units.handoff: Plans need executable representations, so Unit 13 follows meaning through cognitive compilation and search.

units.title: Cognitive Compilation and Semantic IR
units.narrative_job: Explain how intent, relations, constraints, and knowledge can be lowered into efficient executable forms while semantic loss, alternatives, and rescue paths remain visible.
units.central_question: What intermediate representations let different cognitive substrates share work without pretending that structural conformity equals preserved meaning?
units.strongest_objection: Semantic IRs may become brittle private languages that discard nuance while presenting an illusion of interoperability.
units.conclusion_change: End-to-end systems preserving intent, relational roles, and recovery better without explicit IR would narrow the compilation boundary.
units.handoff: Compiled work needs exact, revisable inputs, so Unit 14 develops context transactions and durable semantic memory together.

units.title: Virtual Context and Durable Semantic Memory
units.narrative_job: Separate temporary working context from durable belief while giving both identity, provenance, freshness, taint, rights, contradiction, revocation, and deletion semantics.
units.central_question: How should a system mount what it needs now and preserve what it may need later without treating presence, repetition, or retrieval as truth?
units.strongest_objection: Structured context and memory may amplify early errors and impose false precision while retrieval quality still dominates outcomes.
units.conclusion_change: Simpler retrieval and memory systems matching provenance, contradiction handling, forgetting, transfer, revocation, and cost would justify a thinner layer.
units.handoff: Available information is not necessarily reviewable information, so Unit 15 turns to verification bandwidth and claim custody.

units.title: Verification Bandwidth, Claim Ledgers, and Proof
units.narrative_job: Join reviewer capacity, evidence, defeaters, formal proof, runtime observation, and belief revision without allowing any one of them to stand in for the others.
units.central_question: What must be connected for a claim to remain challengeable, scoped, and correctable as evidence and consumers change?
units.strongest_objection: Rich ledgers and proofs can preserve impeccable metadata around a false or irrelevant conclusion while exhausting review capacity.
units.conclusion_change: Simpler evidence records that produce equal correction, calibration, proof-scope discipline, and consumer repair would justify consolidation.
units.handoff: Accepted claims and plans still need accountable work, so Unit 16 turns the architecture into jobs, work surfaces, and organizations.

units.title: Labor OS, Work Surfaces, and Organizations
units.narrative_job: Explain how humans, agents, tools, and institutions share work without losing task identity, responsibility, recourse, cognitive agency, or the ability to distinguish assistance from organizational replacement.
units.central_question: How does increasingly autonomous AI absorb work surfaces and organizational roles while accountability and human agency remain real?
units.strongest_objection: A labor operating system may bureaucratize work, obscure responsibility in records, and normalize displacement under the label of efficiency.
units.conclusion_change: Conventional issue, CI, organizational, and assistive workflows matching continuity, agency, remedy, and recovery at lower burden would narrow the layer.
units.handoff: Work becomes real through artifacts and effects, which Unit 17 follows through runtime operation and incident recovery.

units.title: Artifact Graphs, Runtime Effects, and Operations
units.narrative_job: Follow owned work into immutable artifacts, least-privilege effects, actual-state observation, incident command, graceful degradation, and recovery without mistaking logs for reality.
units.central_question: Which runtime boundary turns approved proposals into observable effects and keeps the system governable when those effects fail?
units.strongest_objection: Audit and adapter layers can invite rubber-stamping while tools escape declared boundaries and logs omit the effect that matters.
units.conclusion_change: Simpler wrappers and operations systems matching provenance, revocation, incident containment, observation, and recovery would narrow the contract.
units.handoff: One successful operation may become reusable procedure and may cross system boundaries, which Unit 18 governs explicitly.

units.title: Procedural Memory, Inter-Stack Exchange, and Multi-Agent Risk
units.narrative_job: Show how validated work becomes reusable procedure and how procedures, authority, artifacts, and value move between stacks without hiding population-level conflict, collusion, concentration, or systemic failure.
units.central_question: What must accompany a reusable skill or inter-agent transaction so that local validity does not become global permission or systemic safety?
units.strongest_objection: Protocol and procedural formality may not predict emergent behavior and can legitimize harmful markets that satisfy every local rule.
units.conclusion_change: Simpler skill stores and agent protocols that preserve retirement, accountability, dispute, and systemic-risk detection at lower cost would justify consolidation.
units.handoff: Part III asks how the stack chooses its cognitive machinery, learns from experience, and decides when any improvement deserves promotion.

units.title: Routing and Replaceable Cognitive Substrates
units.narrative_job: Make substrate choice a governed routing decision rather than a permanent commitment to transformer monoculture or novelty-driven architecture replacement.
units.central_question: How should a stack choose among general models, specialists, recurrence, cyclic memory, search, tools, and future substrates?
units.strongest_objection: Heterogeneous routing can add coordination cost and correlated failure without outperforming one well-tuned general model.
units.conclusion_change: Matched natural tasks showing no accepted-useful-output advantage after routing, migration, verification, and maintenance costs would favor a simpler substrate strategy.
units.handoff: Selected substrates still need a governed developmental process, which Unit 20 treats as topology over learning rather than only weight updates.

units.title: Governed Training and Learning-Compute Topology
units.narrative_job: Join reproducible training transactions with a topology of learning processes that distinguishes where computation occurs, which state it changes, and how semantic intent survives realization.
units.central_question: How can training remain reproducible and governable when learning spans models, memory, tools, evaluators, environments, and institutions?
units.strongest_objection: The topology layer may redescribe standard training without improving prediction, control, transfer, or cost.
units.conclusion_change: If independent encoders cannot agree on useful topology identity, or matched-resource interventions show no explanatory, control, or outcome value, the layer should be narrowed.
units.handoff: Training produces experiences and candidate lessons; Unit 21 asks which of them should become durable causal structure, where, and for how long.

units.title: Adjudicated Persistence, Generalization, Feedback, Continual Learning, and Unlearning
units.narrative_job: Govern the full path from experience and feedback to a candidate lesson, persistence decision, realization locus, qualification, generalization, forgetting, deletion, and scientific revision.
units.central_question: What durable thing, if any, should change after a system succeeds, fails, receives feedback, or discovers a new regularity?
units.strongest_objection: A persistence adjudicator may add cost and centralize learning decisions that competent local or human-reviewed policies could make more cheaply.
units.conclusion_change: If competent fixed-locus or human-reviewed policies match decision quality, transfer, deletion, and recovery at lower whole-lifecycle cost, the adaptive commit boundary should be narrowed or retired.
units.handoff: A candidate capability or lesson still cannot promote itself, so Unit 22 assembles adversarial evaluation, readiness, thresholds, and assurance.

units.title: Evaluation, Readiness, Thresholds, and Structured Assurance
units.narrative_job: Turn evaluation into a repeated, adversarial, evidence- compiled promotion decision rather than a benchmark score, safety label, or one-time release checklist.
units.central_question: What evidence is sufficient to advance a capability when the candidate may game tests, hide competence, corrupt provenance, or change after evaluation?
units.strongest_objection: Evaluation suites and safety cases can become performative compliance that optimize visible evidence while missing novel or strategic failure.
units.conclusion_change: Leaner readiness methods that detect deception, staleness, provenance failure, and deployment risk equally well under adaptive pressure would justify consolidation.
units.handoff: Evaluation consumes scarce computation and attention, so Unit 23 asks how generation, deliberation, compression, and verification should share a budget.

units.title: Generative Compression and Cognitive Resource Economics
units.narrative_job: Treat faster generation, compact models, artifact compression, and test-time deliberation as competing allocations inside one effect-complete resource decision.
units.central_question: When should a system spend more computation, compress an artifact, use a faster approximation, deliberate, verify, or fall back?
units.strongest_objection: Detailed resource accounting may be expensive, misestimated, and easy to game, producing optimization theater rather than useful allocation.
units.conclusion_change: Matched effect-complete studies showing static budgets or one general model equal or outperform governed allocation would narrow the resource layer.
units.handoff: Cognitive cost is realized on physical infrastructure, which Unit 24 treats as an architectural and governance constraint rather than a footnote.

units.title: Physical Compute, Energy, and Infrastructure
units.narrative_job: Connect abstract cognitive budgets to hardware, memory, networks, energy, cooling, supply chains, resilience, environmental burden, local ownership, and edge or federated alternatives.
units.central_question: What physical and social constraints determine whether an efficient cognitive architecture is actually deployable, resilient, and worth its displaced costs?
units.strongest_objection: Physical-impact accounting is context-dependent and may overstate architectural control over grid, supply-chain, and institutional outcomes.
units.conclusion_change: Deployment studies showing physical constraints and topology do not materially affect accepted useful output, resilience, privacy, or total cost would narrow this layer.
units.handoff: Once the stack can change itself and its physical deployment, Unit 25 confronts recursive improvement, replication, and containment directly.

units.title: Recursive Improvement, Replication, and Containment
units.narrative_job: Show how a stack may generate, test, and adopt improvements without letting proposal become ratification, local gain become descendant authority, or replication escape containment and retirement.
units.central_question: What boundaries let a system improve recursively while remaining interruptible, evidence-bound, and unable to authorize its own proliferation?
units.strongest_objection: Governance layers may be bypassed by a sufficiently capable improver, while restrictive containment may prevent the very progress the system is meant to enable.
units.conclusion_change: Competing architectures that achieve equal improvement, reversibility, descendant control, and incident recovery with fewer authority boundaries would justify simplification.
units.handoff: The final unit must show the whole architecture operating as one system and explain how Project Theseus and the Living Book keep it testable.

units.title: Integrated Reference Architecture, Project Theseus, and the Living Research Method
units.narrative_job: Reassemble the book into an effect-complete reference path, show how Project Theseus implements and challenges it, and make the Living Book the mechanism by which claims, proofs, experiments, prose, and open questions remain corrigible.
units.central_question: What does it mean to implement the ASI Stack as a testable system rather than merely describe an attractive architecture?
units.strongest_objection: The integrated architecture may be internally coherent yet too costly, incomplete, or weakly evidenced to outperform simpler agent systems; Project Theseus may validate only its own conventions.
units.conclusion_change: Fresh-checkout natural tasks, independent reproduction, governance-rent ablations, and end-to-end failure tests that favor a simpler system would narrow or reject the reference design.
units.handoff: The book closes with a maintained research frontier: every open claim has an owner, a strongest objection, an evidence path, and an explicit condition under which the architecture should change.

non_claims: This maintained draft is not a major-version release or a generated excerpt of the live technical chapters.
A routed owner does not transfer claim, proof, source, evidence, or authority ownership to the Human Reader unit.
Word-count or render completion is not editorial approval, evidence, safety, readiness, AGI, or ASI.
